newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani rupee ends down in kerb, seen stable.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani rupee ends down in kerb, seen stable.

text.p: The Pakistani rupee ended 0.02 down at 42.00 to the dollar in the kerb market on Tuesday amid low buying of the U.S. currency before Friday's 1997/98 (July-June) budget, dealers said.
The rupee was likely to open stable on Wednesday, a dealer said.
The State (central) Bank of Pakistan rupee rate, last changed on May 23, was 40.3900/40.5920 against the dollar.
The premium on the foreign exchange bearer certificates closed at 3.90 percent compared to the opening at 4.00 percent.
